item.title: Effort, Fast Mode, and Thinking - AI's 'Thinking Depth' Control Knob
item.description: Deep dive into Claude Code's reasoning control mechanisms: Effort levels, Fast Mode acceleration, and Thinking mode - plus how to adjust AI thinking depth based on task complexity.

item.title: Function Tool Performance Optimization: Timeout, Concurrency, and Resource Management
item.description: Detailed Function Tool performance optimization strategies: timeout control, concurrent calls, connection pool management, and how to prevent slow Tools from affecting entire Agent's response.

item.title: Why Does Async Rust Feel So Hard? A Deep Dive for Developers
item.description: Async Rust is powerful but frustrating. From ecosystem fragmentation and Pin/Unpin to cancellation safety and performance traps, this article breaks down the real pain points with visual diagrams and practical analogies.

item.title: Go 2026 Survival Guide for Backend Engineers: The Changes That Actually Affect Production
item.description: Go 1.25 and 1.26 bring container-aware GOMAXPROCS, go fix overhaul, Green Tea GC, testing/synctest, and more. A practical breakdown of what backend engineers actually need to know.

item.title: PostgreSQL 18 UUIDv7: Your Indexes Can Finally Breathe
item.description: PostgreSQL 18 brings native UUIDv7 support with 50% index performance improvement. Say goodbye to UUIDv4 fragmentation and get primary keys that are both ordered and unique.

item.title: Stop Blaming Your Database — It's Your Pagination That's Slow
item.description: Database queries getting slower as users scroll deeper? OFFSET pagination is the culprit more often than not. Here's why and what to do about it.

item.title: The Trouble with JavaScript Streams: What Web Streams API Got Wrong
item.description: Web Streams API locked you out? BYOB mode giving you headaches? Node.js core contributor James Snell proposed an alternative using async iterables, with 2x to 120x performance gains. See how pull vs push models affect your code performance.

item.title: PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark Data: I Said You Could Kill Your Redis Cache Layer. You Didn't Believe Me.
item.description: Real benchmark data for PostgreSQL 18: async IO + skip scan deliver a massive database performance leap. Production test with 1K concurrent users shows P95 latency dropping from 72ms to 54ms after removing Redis. Third-party benchmarks show 3.4x faster sequential scans.

item.title: PostgreSQL Query Parsing Too Slow? PgDog Ditched Protobuf and Got 5x Faster
item.description: PgDog is a Rust-based PostgreSQL proxy. They discovered Protobuf serialization was the real bottleneck in SQL query parsing — not the Postgres parser itself. By replacing Protobuf with direct C-to-Rust FFI bindings, they achieved 5-10x faster parsing.

item.title: The C10M Problem in 2026: Why Your 128-Core Server Still Can't Handle 10 Million Packets Per Second
item.description: When packet rates surpass 2 million per second, the Linux network stack simply gives up. It's like your doorbell won't stop ringing, but you never have time to open the door. Let's talk about bypassing the kernel.

item.title: The Rust Async Trap Everyone Steps On Once
item.description: It compiles. It runs. It even passes stress tests... until production catches fire. Let's talk about that classic async Rust pitfall everyone hits.

item.title: gRPC is 10x Faster Than REST? Why Your Team Hasn't Switched
item.description: gRPC can indeed be much faster than REST, but most teams are right to stick with REST. Let's talk about the real cost behind the speed.

item.title: Frontend Performance Optimization: I Replaced Axios With 25 Lines of Vanilla JS
item.description: Discovered that 13KB Axios is just a fetch wrapper. Using 25 lines of vanilla JS to achieve the same functionality while reducing bundle size by 92%. A real frontend performance optimization case.

item.title: PostgreSQL 18 vs Redis: The Day I Realized Our Cache Layer Was Optional
item.description: PostgreSQL 18's async IO and skip scan made our database so fast that Redis caching became optional. Three engineers independently deleted 4,000+ lines of cache code in a single week.

item.title: The Memory Layout Trick That Turns Rust Structs Into Cache Miss Monsters
item.description: Think field order doesn't matter? Wrong. How you arrange fields in a Rust struct can make your code 10x slower. Let's talk about memory alignment, padding, and CPU cache with a suitcase packing analogy.

item.title: The Secret to 10x Rust Performance: Stop Cloning, Start Borrowing
item.description: Why is your Rust code running like a snail? You might be using clone() too much. This article explains how Rust's borrowing system can transform your code from sluggish to blazing fast.

item.title: Python Finally Got Fast: JIT Compiler Makes Code Performance Take Off
item.description: Python 3.15 introduces a native JIT compiler that delivers 20% performance improvements without changing a single line of code. Here's how to enable this experimental feature.

item.title: Rust 1.90 Upgrade Crash Report: My Codebase Didn't Make It
item.description: Performance tanked after upgrading to Rust 1.90? Here's why and how to claw it back.

item.title: Will WASM + Rust Replace Linux Containers? Performance, Security, Cold Starts, and Trade‑offs
item.description: Plain‑English notes and references for WASM + Rust vs Linux containers: performance, security, cold starts, ecosystem, and standards.

item.title: Agno-Go: Building AI Agents in Go - What's it Like Being 16x Faster than Python?
item.description: Rewriting AI Agent framework in Go brings 16x performance boost, 180ns agent startup, and only 1.2KB memory footprint - this is the extreme experience Agno-Go delivers

item.title: A Survival Guide to Zig Performance Profiling on Apple Silicon (M1/M2)
item.description: Performance profiling for Zig on Apple Silicon (M1/M2) can be challenging as common tools like perf and valgrind are not supported. This guide introduces alternatives like Samply, poop, and Tracy to help you analyze and optimize your Zig code on macOS.

item.title: Rust System Design: These Three Libraries Quietly Do the Dirty Work (And Many Devs Still Don’t Know)
item.description: Tokio, Crossbeam, and Rkyv: three crates that make concurrency, state sharing, and serialization dramatically simpler in Rust.

item.title: Rust Async: 7 Common Mistakes That Kill Performance and Cause Crashes
item.description: A deep dive into 7 common Rust async programming pitfalls, such as blocking threads, incorrect lock usage, and mishandled Futures. Learn to avoid these mistakes with practical examples to write high-performance, stable asynchronous code.

item.title: Rust's Lazy Iterators Explained: Avoiding Common Pitfalls
item.description: A deep dive into Rust's lazy iterators. Uncover common performance pitfalls and beginner mistakes related to lazy evaluation. Learn to use methods like map, filter, and collect efficiently to write high-performance Rust code.
